correctness.rationale: A C^4 graph f(x)=a x^2+b x^3+c x^4+o(x^4) with a>0 has inverse signed-square-root branch x(z)=z-b z^2/(2a)+(5b^2/(8a^2)-c/(2a))z^3+o(z^3). This yields chord width L(y)=2 sqrt(y/a)[1+q y+o(y)], q=5b^2/(8a^3)-c/(2a^2). Exact Fubini moment integrals give d/h=3/5+12q h/175+o(h), which equals 3/5-(3f''f''''-5f'''^2)h/(525 f''^3)+o(h). Area normalization yields the stated constant times the standard equiaffine curvature. The conic sign comparison follows from the exact discriminant and monotone covariance. The standalone checker passed conic and asymmetric quartic samples; no numerical test replaces analytic steps.

value.rationale: The theorem solves a natural inverse-geometric question for the Archimedean section centroid: the first nonuniversal coefficient of an directly measurable depth ratio determines the signed equiaffine curvature at every positive-curvature C^4 point. Its area^(2/3) normalization makes the answer equiaffine-covariant, it separates the local ellipse/parabola/hyperbola signs, and it is not just a restatement of the known 3/5 limit or a numerical invariant with no geometric use.
